title: Amazon FBA Product Photos: Complete Image Checklist | edit-photo
heading: Amazon Product Image Checklist for FBA Sellers
description: Plan and review Amazon product images with a practical checklist covering the main image, secondary images, product details, scale, packaging, context shots, and pre-upload QA.

blocks.text: A complete Amazon product image set should help a shopper identify the item, understand what is included, judge important details, estimate size, and see how the product fits into a real situation. The main image starts that job, but the rest of the image sequence must answer the questions that remain.

This checklist focuses on planning the full image set and reviewing it before upload. It does not replace Amazon's current category requirements, guarantee acceptance, or promise a sales outcome. Check Seller Central before publishing because marketplace rules and available image features can change.
What an Amazon product image set should accomplish

items.label: Identify
items.text: Show the actual product clearly and make the main purchase option easy to recognize.

items.label: Explain
items.text: Use secondary images to show details, materials, controls, dimensions, packaging, and included items.

items.label: Provide context
items.text: Help shoppers understand scale and intended use without implying accessories or results that are not included.

items.label: Stay consistent
items.text: Keep product color, orientation, crop logic, typography, and visual treatment coherent across the listing.

items.label: Pass review
items.text: Check every export against the current rules for the relevant product category and marketplace.

blocks.text: Main image preparation

Treat the main image as a precise identification image, not the entire sales presentation. Start with a sharp source photo, preserve every product edge, verify what belongs in the frame, and prepare the required background and crop only after the product cutout has been checked.

Do not copy old dimensions, product-coverage percentages, file formats, or zoom thresholds from an earlier listing without checking Amazon's current guidance. Requirements can vary by category and marketplace.
For the detailed main-image background workflow and current-rule checkpoints,
blocks.label: use the Amazon white-background photo guide

blocks.text: When you are ready to prepare the white-background working file,
blocks.label: open the Amazon image preparation tool

blocks.text: Secondary image sequence

There is no useful one-size-fits-all sequence. Choose each secondary image because it answers a buyer question that the main image cannot. A simple product may need fewer explanations than a configurable, technical, wearable, or multi-part item.

blocks.caption: Build the sequence around buyer questions rather than a fixed image count.

cells: Alternate view
What does the back, side, top, or underside look like?
Same product variant, consistent orientation, no missing parts
Detail view
What are the important materials, controls, finishes, or construction details?
Sharp focus and truthful detail
Scale view
How large is the product in a familiar context?
Readable dimensions and no misleading perspective
Included-items view
Exactly what arrives with the order?
Every shown item is included or clearly identified
Context view
Where and how is the product normally used?
Plausible setting without unsupported performance claims

blocks.text: Product details and close-ups

Use close-ups for details that affect selection or use: texture, finish, connectors, closures, labels, controls, stitching, ingredients, or craftsmanship. Keep enough surrounding product visible that the shopper can understand where the detail belongs.

items.text: Prioritize details that distinguish variants or answer common pre-purchase questions.
Check that the close-up belongs to the exact color, size, model, and bundle shown on the listing.
Avoid enlarging a soft crop until compression artifacts look like product texture.

blocks.text: Size and scale

A shopper should not have to infer scale from the main image crop. Use a dimension graphic created in an appropriate layout tool, a truthful in-context photograph, or a comparison with a familiar object when current category rules allow it. Keep units readable and make sure perspective does not exaggerate size.
Packaging and included items

Show packaging when it matters for gifting, storage, authenticity, assembly, or delivery expectations. Use a separate included-items image for sets, accessories, cables, refills, and components. Do not add props that can be mistaken for part of the order.
Lifestyle and context images

Context images should demonstrate normal use, environment, fit, or scale. Photograph the actual product in a suitable setting and review every visible accessory, person, label, and screen. edit-photo does not generate lifestyle scenes or replace objects inside a photograph; create or license those images separately.
Image consistency across the listing
Consistency makes the set easier to scan, but it should not erase useful differences between image roles. Compare the full sequence as thumbnails and at full size.

items.label: Composition
items.text: Keep repeated angles, margins, and orientation deliberate rather than almost aligned.

items.label: Lighting
items.text: Check that highlights and shadows describe the same product accurately across the set.

items.label: Color
items.text: Compare the product with a reliable reference and investigate unexplained color shifts between photos.

items.label: Graphics
items.text: If permitted, use one readable hierarchy and consistent units, labels, and spacing.

items.label: Variant accuracy
items.text: Do not mix images from different colors, sizes, bundles, revisions, or regional packaging.

blocks.text: Background and edge QA

When an image needs isolation, background removal is only the first pass. Compare the cutout with the source and inspect the outer contour, holes, handles, cables, transparent regions, and fine product parts. Check for retained background, halos, missing edges, and accidental transparency.
For a focused cutout and manual-edge review workflow,
blocks.label: use the product background remover

blocks.text: Keep a reusable source asset when more than one channel export is needed;
blocks.label: learn when to use a transparent PNG master

blocks.text: Color and lighting review

Review color and lighting against the physical product and the original files. Watch for mixed white balance, clipped highlights, blocked shadows, screen glare, and inconsistent exposure. These are capture or color-editing issues: edit-photo removes backgrounds and supports edge inspection, but it does not calibrate color, relight products, repair blur, or correct exposure automatically.
File and export checks

Export from the best available source rather than a marketplace screenshot. Open the final file after export and inspect it at normal viewing size and at 100% zoom. Confirm that compression, resizing, flattening, and color-profile changes have not introduced visible damage. Then compare file dimensions, format, naming, and upload limits with Amazon's current requirements for the target marketplace.
Pre-upload checklist

blocks.caption: Run this review on the complete set before uploading or replacing listing images.

cells: Listing match
Is every image for the correct ASIN, variant, bundle, and packaging version?
Return to the source selection and replace mismatched assets
Sequence
Does each image answer a different useful buyer question?
Remove repetition and fill the most important information gap
Product accuracy
Are colors, proportions, included items, and visible claims truthful?
Reshoot or correct the source in an appropriate editor
Edge quality
Are contours, openings, transparent areas, and fine details intact?
Return to the cutout and manually inspect the affected edge
Consistency
Do orientation, lighting, crop logic, units, and graphic treatment feel intentional?
Compare the set side by side and standardize only what should match
Current rules
Does every file meet today's category and marketplace requirements?
Verify in Seller Central before upload

blocks.text: When to use the white background guide

Use the white-background guide when the unresolved task is specifically the Amazon MAIN image: background preparation, product crop, transparent-versus-white output, or current main-image requirements. Keep those detailed rules there so this Hub can focus on the complete listing image set.
Review the focused workflow in
blocks.label: the Amazon white-background checklist

blocks.text: When to use the suppression troubleshooting guide

Use the suppression guide only after Amazon reports an image-related listing problem. Start with the exact message in Seller Central, identify the affected image, and avoid rebuilding the whole set until the reported issue is understood.
If an existing listing has already been affected,
blocks.label: follow the image-suppression troubleshooting guide

items.question: How many images should an Amazon product listing have?
items.answer: Use enough permitted images to answer the important buyer questions for that product without repeating the same information. Check the current image availability and requirements in Seller Central rather than relying on a fixed universal number.

items.question: Should every Amazon image use a white background?
items.answer: The main image and secondary images serve different jobs, and current requirements can differ by image role and category. Use the dedicated white-background guide for main-image preparation and verify the current rules before upload.

items.question: What should secondary product images show?
items.answer: Choose views that add new information, such as alternate angles, important details, dimensions, scale, packaging, included items, and truthful context. The right sequence depends on the product.

items.question: Can edit-photo create the complete Amazon image set?
items.answer: No. edit-photo removes image backgrounds, supports cutout-edge inspection, and exports reusable assets. It does not generate lifestyle scenes, design A+ Content, create complex listing graphics, relight products, or calibrate color.

items.question: What is the final check before uploading Amazon product photos?
items.answer: Confirm the correct product and variant, review the whole sequence for accuracy and consistency, inspect every exported file, and compare it with Amazon's current requirements for the relevant marketplace and category.

cta.title: Prepare a reusable product cutout
cta.description: Remove the original background, inspect the product edge, and keep a reusable asset for the marketplace exports in your image plan.
